arxiv-2107-07599.title: Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) and Robotics
arxiv-2107-07599.creator: Hanna Kurniawati
arxiv-2107-07599.description: Abstract Planning under uncertainty is critical to robotics. The Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) is a mathematical framework for such planning problems. It is powerful due to its careful quantification of the non-deterministic effects of actions and partial observability of the states.

arxiv-2201-02302.title: Extending One-Stage Detection with Open-World Proposals
arxiv-2201-02302.creator: Sachin Konan, Kevin J Liang, Li Yin
arxiv-2201-02302.description: Abstract In many applications, such as autonomous driving, hand manipulation, or robot navigation, object detection methods must be able to detect objects unseen in the training set. Open World Detection (OWD) seeks to tackle this problem by generalizing detection performance to seen and unseen class categories.

arxiv-2307-02392.title: RADiff: Controllable Diffusion Models for Radio Astronomical Maps Generation
arxiv-2307-02392.creator: Renato Sortino, Thomas Cecconello, Andrea DeMarco, Giuseppe Fiameni, Andrea Pilzer, Andrew M. Hopkins, Daniel Magro, Simone Riggi, Eva Sciacca, Adriano Ingallinera, Cristobal Bordiu, Filomena Bufano, Concetto Spampinato
arxiv-2307-02392.description: Abstract Along with the nearing completion of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), comes an increasing demand for accurate and reliable automated solutions to extract valuable information from the vast amount of data it will allow acquiring. Automated source finding is a particularly important task in this context, as it enables the detection and classification of astronomical objects.

arxiv-2308-04623.title: Accelerating LLM Inference with Staged Speculative Decoding
arxiv-2308-04623.creator: Benjamin Spector, Chris Re
arxiv-2308-04623.description: Abstract Recent advances with large language models (LLM) illustrate their diverse capabilities. We propose a novel algorithm, staged speculative decoding, to accelerate LLM inference in small-batch, on-device scenarios. We address the low arithmetic intensity of small-batch inference by improving upon previous work in speculative decoding.

arxiv-2311-10611.title: TacFR-Gripper: A Reconfigurable Fin Ray-Based Compliant Robotic Gripper with Tactile Skin for In-Hand Manipulation
arxiv-2311-10611.creator: Qingzheng Cong, Wen Fan, Dandan Zhang
arxiv-2311-10611.description: Abstract This paper introduces the TacFR-Gripper, a reconfigurable Fin Ray-based soft and compliant robotic gripper equipped with tactile skin, which can be used for dexterous in-hand manipulation tasks. This gripper can adaptively grasp objects of diverse shapes and stiffness levels.

arxiv-2312-09427.title: The doubly asymmetric simple exclusion process, the colored Boolean process, and the restricted random growth model
arxiv-2312-09427.creator: Yuhan Jiang
arxiv-2312-09427.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuhan Jiang. The multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process (mASEP) is a Markov chain in which particles of different species hop along a one-dimensional lattice. This paper studies the doubly asymmetric simple exclusion process DASEP ⁡ ( n , p , q ) \DASEP(n,p,q) in which q q particles with species 1 , … , p 1,\dots,p hop along a circular lattice with n sites, but also the particles are allowed to spontaneously change from one species to another.

arxiv-2403-03792.title: Neural Exec : Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
arxiv-2403-03792.creator: Dario Pasquini, Martin Strohmeier, Carmela Troncoso
arxiv-2403-03792.description: Abstract . We introduce a new family of prompt injection attacks, termed Neural Exec . Unlike known attacks that rely on handcrafted strings (e.g., Ignore previous instructions and... ), we show that it is possible to conceptualize the creation of execution triggers as a differentiable search problem and use learning-based methods to autonomously generate them.

arxiv-2504-16042.title: Approximate matrices of systems of max-min fuzzy relational equations
arxiv-2504-16042.creator: Ismaïl Baaj LEMMA, Paris-Panthéon-Assas University, Paris, 75006, France ismail.baaj@assas-universite.fr
arxiv-2504-16042.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ismaïl Baaj LEMMA, Paris-Panthéon-Assas University, Paris, 75006, France ismail.baaj@assas-universite.fr. In this article, we address the inconsistency of a system of max-min fuzzy relational equations by minimally modifying the matrix governing the system in order to achieve consistency.

arxiv-2601-08524.title: Revisiting the Great Attractor: The Local Group’s streamline trajectory, cosmic velocity and dynamical fate
arxiv-2601-08524.creator: Richard Stiskalek, Harry Desmond, Stuart McAlpine, Guilhem Lavaux, Jens Jasche, Michael J. Hudson
arxiv-2601-08524.description: Abstract We revisit the Great Attractor using the Manticore-Local suite of digital twins of the nearby Universe. The Great Attractor concept has been proposed as an answer to three distinct questions: what sources the Local Group velocity in the cosmic microwave background frame, where present-day velocity streamlines converge, and where the Local Group is moving to.

arxiv-2601-21994.title: Superconducting properties of transition metal dichalcogenides in proximity to a conventional superconductor
arxiv-2601-21994.creator: Florian Kayatz, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, Jorge Cayao
arxiv-2601-21994.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Florian Kayatz, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, Jorge Cayao. Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold relevance for spin-triplet superconducting phases due to their inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling, but the majority of studies have so far focused on oversimplified models. In this work, we consider a TMD monolayer using a three-orbital model with anisotropic couplings and investigate the emergent superconducting properties when it is placed in proximity to a conventional spin-singlet s s -wave superconductor.

pmc-10671640.title: Detection Rate and Spectrum of Pathogenic Variations in a Cohort of 83 Patients with Suspected Hereditary Risk of Kidney Cancer
pmc-10671640.creator: Zangbéwendé Guy Ouedraogo, Florian Ceruti, Mathis Lepage, Mathilde Gay-Bellile, Nancy Uhrhammer, Flora Ponelle-Chachuat, Yannick Bidet, Maud Privat, Mathias Cavaillé, Andrew Mallett
pmc-10671640.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Hereditary predisposition to cancer affects about 3–5% of renal cancers. Testing criteria have been proposed in France for genetic testing of non-syndromic renal cancer. Our study explores the detection rates associated with our testing criteria. Using a comprehensive gene panel including 8 genes related to renal cancer and 50 genes related to hereditary predisposition to other cancers, we evaluated the detection rate of pathogenic variants in a cohort of 83 patients with suspected renal cancer predisposition.

pmc-10738622.title: LIFE-COURSE AND CONTEXTUAL FACTORS OF ADVANCE CARE PLANNING AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH LIMITED INCOME
pmc-10738622.creator: Christine Kimpel, Jana Lauderdale, David Schlundt, Mary Dietrich, Amy Ratcliff, Cathy Maxwell
pmc-10738622.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundCumulative disadvantage across the lifespan can lead to income, health, and advance care planning (ACP) disparities, resulting in increased caregiver decisional distress and reduced healthcare equity during times of cognitive incapacity. ACP is the process of patient and familial learning, communication, and documentation of life-sustaining care and quality of life preferences after personal reflection, but ACP rates remain lower among older adults with limited income.

pmc-11312090.title: Age-Related Retinal Layer Thickness Changes Measured by OCT in APPNL-F/NL-F Mice: Implications for Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11312090.creator: Lidia Sánchez-Puebla, Rosa de Hoz, Elena Salobrar-García, Alberto Arias-Vázquez, María González-Jiménez, Ana I. Ramírez, José A. Fernández-Albarral, José A. Matamoros, Lorena Elvira-Hurtado, Takaomi C. Saido, Takashi Saito, Carmen Nieto Vaquero, María I. Cuartero, María A. Moro, Juan J. Salazar, Iné
pmc-11312090.description: In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), transgenic mouse models have established links between abnormalities in the retina and those in the brain. APPNL-F/NL-F is a murine, humanized AD model that replicates several pathological features observed in patients with AD. Research has focused on obtaining quantitative parameters from optical coherence tomography (OCT) in AD.

pmc-11455894.title: Nuclear PCGF3 inhibits the antiviral immune response by suppressing the interferon-stimulated gene
pmc-11455894.creator: Gula Da, Junmin Wang, Jing Shang, Cuiping Xun, Yang Yu, Yong Wang, Ning Tie, Hongbin Li
pmc-11455894.description: Type I interferon (IFN-I) plays a crucial role in the antiviral immune response and inflammatory autoimmune diseases by inducing the expression of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs). Hence, the regulation of ISG expression is fundamental for maintaining immune homeostasis. In this study, we found that PCGF3 negatively regulates the antiviral response by suppressing the expression of ISGs.

pmc-11498318.title: Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis (SSC): An Underrecognized Complication of Severe COVID-19 Pneumonitis
pmc-11498318.creator: Mariya Pogorelova, Victoria Kusztos
pmc-11498318.description: COVID-19-secondary sclerosing cholangitis (COVID-SSC) is a distinct subset of secondary sclerosing cholangitis in critically ill patients (SSC-CIP) that presents after COVID-19 infection with alkaline phosphatase predominant elevation of liver enzymes. COVID-SSC typically presents within three months of COVID-19 diagnosis and most commonly occurs following severe COVID-19 infection.

pmc-12513979.title: Sinomenine Hydrochloride Impedes Memory Impairments via Nrf2/HO-1-Mediated Inhibition of Oxidative Stress, Neuroinflammation and Apoptosis in Mice Brain
pmc-12513979.creator: Waqar Ali, Kyonghwan Choe, Inayat Ur Rehman, Hyun Young Park, Sihoon Jang, Safi Ullah, Tae Ju Park, Myeong Ok Kim
pmc-12513979.description: Oxidative stress is a key factor in the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders. We evaluated whether sinomenine hydrochloride (SH) exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects against cadmium chloride (CdCl2)-induced neurodegeneration and synaptic impairment in mouse brains. The mice were allowed to undergo Cd injection for two weeks.

pmc-12581482.title: Estimating the burden of adult diabetes in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis with attributable risk assessment
pmc-12581482.creator: Rui Wang, Shuoming Luo, Peng Wang, Meihui Yu, Zhenglu Liu, Jiabi Qin, Yang Xiao, Xia Li, Zhiguang Zhou
pmc-12581482.description: BackgroundDiabetes represents a significant public health challenge in China. This comprehensive meta-analysis systematically investigated temporal patterns in diabetes prevalence and evaluated key modifiable risk factors among Chinese adults over a 20-year period (2000–2020).MethodsWe conducted a systematic search across six major electronic databases to identify population-based epidemiological studies reporting diabetes prevalence and/or associated modifiable risk factors.

pmc-12735735.title: MicroRNA Signatures and Machine Learning Models for Predicting Cardiotoxicity in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Patients
pmc-12735735.creator: Maria Anastasiou, Evangelos Oikonomou, Panagiotis Theofilis, Maria Gazouli, George-Angelos Papamikroulis, Athina Goliopoulou, Vasiliki Tsigkou, Vasiliki Skandami, Angeliki Margoni, Kyriaki Cholidou, Amanda Psyrri, Konstantinos Tsioufis, Flora Zagouri, Gerasimos Siasos, Dimitris Tousoulis, László Kőh
pmc-12735735.description: Background: HER2-positive breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy and targeted therapy (including anthracyclines and trastuzumab) face an elevated risk of cardiotoxicity, which can lead to long-term cardiovascular complications. Identifying predictive biomarkers is essential for early intervention. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), known regulators of gene expression and cardiovascular function, have emerged as potential indicators of cardiotoxicity.

pmc-12739458.title: Awareness, Perceptions, Willingness, and Feasibility of mHealth Apps Among People Living With Epilepsy: Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study
pmc-12739458.creator: Bushra Batool Zahra, Muhammad Amir Hamza, Rehana Sarwat, Hina Batool Zahra, Ayesha Azam, Ali Ahmed
pmc-12739458.description: BackgroundThe rapid expansion of mobile health (mHealth) apps has transformed health care delivery worldwide. Despite their potential to improve epilepsy care, a substantial treatment gap remains, especially in low- and middle-income countries, due to limited resources, stigma, and low adoption of digital technologies.

pmc-12831266.title: Maternal food literacy and health behaviors in relation to children’s DMFT scores: a cross-sectional study from Türkiye
pmc-12831266.creator: Yavuzalp Solak, Gün Burak Tek, Hasan Durmuş, Erhan Kaya, Sevim Tek
pmc-12831266.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOral health in childhood is influenced by parental literacy, dietary practices, and hygiene behaviors. Maternal food literacy may play a critical role in shaping children’s oral health, yet this relationship remains underexplored in low- and middle-income settings.

pmc-13065598.title: From meta-analysis to knowledge graphs: reimagining social isolation research in older adults
pmc-13065598.creator: Zian Shou, Yisheng Liang, Chang Lin, Yibo He
pmc-13065598.description: adults. By exclusively focusing on individuals aged 65 years and above, this study addresses a critical gap in existing literature, which has mostly targeted general adult populations, thereby providing strong evidence for understanding how social determinants shape health outcomes in the aging demographic. Nevertheless, we wish to offer several constructive advice.

pmc-13343700.title: Qishen Granules attenuate adverse ventricular remodeling in chronic heart failure by promoting Legumain/Arg1/Rac1-mediated efferocytosis of resident cardiac macrophages
pmc-13343700.creator: Meijiao Tao, Shixuan Min, Jiali Liu, Huishi Xiao, Tong Xiao, Sisi Liang, Xin Liu, Jun Wang, Yulin Ouyang, Ruijia Wen, Lei Wang, Wei Wang, Yao Zhang, Chun Li
pmc-13343700.description: BackgroundVentricular remodeling is a key pathological feature of chronic heart failure (CHF). Following myocardial infarction (MI), impaired macrophage efferocytosis sustains cardiac inflammation, disrupts tissue repair, and accelerates adverse remodeling and dysfunction. Qishen Granules (QSG) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine formulation used in the clinical treatment of heart failure.

pmc-13416219.creator: Daniel E. Ho, Julian Nyarko, Vanessa Parli, Christopher D. Manning

pmc-13590089.title: Therapeutic potential of a novel virulent bacteriophage XQ-1 against avian pathogenic Escherichia coli infection in broiler chickens
pmc-13590089.creator: Yuqing Duan, Changchun Gao, Xi Yang, Pei Zhu, Jinping Wang, Yun Zhou, Zihan Yang, Yitong Guo, Guangming Tian, Jiaying Liu, Xiaowei Fang, Lei Tan, Mengting Zuo, Jun Yao
pmc-13590089.description: Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) represents a significant subgroup within extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli strains and constitutes a substantial threat to the global poultry industry. Although the negative impacts of APEC have been mitigated considerably through antibiotic use, this practice has concurrently facilitated the widespread emergence and dissemination of antibiotic-resistant APEC strains worldwide.

pmc-13729933.title: Inclusion Complexations of Levamisole and Cocaine With Molecular Baskets. Fluorescence Displacement Assay for Detection of Cocaine and Its Adulterant Levamisole in Aqueous Media
pmc-13729933.creator: Christopher T Mortensen, Carson E Ward, Nitesh Kumar, Logan Willemann, Ryan Lutz, Kailey Hughes, Zheng Zheng, Jovica D Badjić
pmc-13729933.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We investigated inclusion complexation of levamisole (LEV+), a common adulterant of cocaine (COC+), with six molecular baskets 1 3− –6 18− of increasing cavity depth and anionic charge at the portal. 1H NMR and mass spectrometry showed that 1 3− to 6 18− bind to LEV+ to form binary complexes in water, with the stability increasing across the series and highest for dendritic basket 6 18− (K d = 10 µM).
